fixes.explanation: You got it, baker! God says, “…go to the land I will show you.” In His words to Abram, the place isn't named, only the promise that He will show him. That takes real trust, friend. I'd have asked for directions twice and then packed extra cookie boxes.

You got it, baker! Abram travels through the land as far as the Oak of Moreh at Shechem (Genesis 12:6). Then the text says, “And at that time the Canaanites were in the land.” So the land has people in it already. Abram shows up as the new face in town, and I bet he didn't know where the good parking was.

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
The place is named earlier in the passage: Terah’s family set out for Canaan in Genesis 11:31. God does not name the destination in His instruction to Abram in Genesis 12:1.
